questions.stem: Which electromagnetic principle does a dynamic microphone use to convert sound into an electrical signal?

options.text: Static electricity
Electromagnetic induction
The heating effect of a current
The motor effect

questions.explanation: A dynamic microphone uses electromagnetic induction (the generator effect). Sound waves cause the diaphragm and attached coil to move in a magnetic field, inducing a voltage in the coil.

questions.stem: Which electromagnetic principle does a loudspeaker use to convert electrical signals into sound?

options.text: The motor effect
Electromagnetic induction
Lenz's law
The right-hand grip rule

questions.explanation: A loudspeaker uses the motor effect. An alternating current flows through a voice coil in a magnetic field, creating a force that makes the coil and attached cone vibrate, producing sound waves.

questions.stem: In a dynamic microphone, what is attached to the diaphragm?

options.text: A permanent magnet
A transformer
A battery
A coil of wire

questions.explanation: In a dynamic microphone, a coil of wire is attached to the diaphragm. When sound waves cause the diaphragm to vibrate, the coil moves within the magnetic field of a fixed permanent magnet, inducing a voltage.

questions.stem: Why does a microphone produce a larger voltage when a louder sound is detected?

options.text: Because the resistance of the coil decreases
Because the permanent magnet becomes stronger
Because louder sounds have a higher frequency
Because the diaphragm moves further and faster, so the coil cuts through more field lines per second

questions.explanation: A louder sound has a larger amplitude, causing the diaphragm to move further and faster. The coil attached to it therefore moves more rapidly through the magnetic field, inducing a larger voltage.

questions.stem: What determines the pitch of the sound produced by a loudspeaker?

options.text: The strength of the permanent magnet
The frequency of the alternating current signal
The thickness of the wire in the voice coil
The size of the loudspeaker cone

questions.explanation: The pitch of the sound produced by a loudspeaker is determined by the frequency of the AC signal. The cone vibrates at the same frequency as the electrical signal, producing sound waves of that frequency.

questions.stem: How are a microphone and a loudspeaker related?

options.text: They are essentially the same device working in reverse
They use completely different physical principles
They both use the motor effect
A loudspeaker cannot function as a microphone under any circumstances

questions.explanation: A microphone and a loudspeaker are essentially the same device working in reverse. Both contain a coil and a permanent magnet. A loudspeaker can even generate a small voltage when its cone is pushed, acting as a crude microphone.

questions.stem: In a loudspeaker, why must the electrical signal be AC rather than DC?

options.text: Because AC is safer than DC
Because DC would damage the voice coil
Because AC causes the cone to vibrate back and forth, producing sound waves
Because DC cannot flow through a coil

questions.explanation: AC alternates direction, causing the force on the voice coil to reverse repeatedly. This makes the cone vibrate back and forth, pushing and pulling on the air to create sound waves. DC would push the cone in one direction only.
